messages:
incident-bot: [P1] ORION (prod, VPC) — us-west-2 dedicated pool reports spike in 5xx + token timeouts. impact: request failures for pinned tenant orion-prod. Paging oncall.
Alice Ng: paging in. seeing elevated 5xx rate ~8% and tail latency > 4s for orion-prod. Cloud metrics show some GPU nodes with OOM/restarts in dedicated pool.
Ben Turner: copying infra. any immediate mitigation plan? can we route ORION traffic off the failing nodes to fallback capacity?
Carla Diaz: I can set a tenant override to a safe model variant (smaller quantized) for Orion while we stabilize. Suggest pin to orion/safe-1.3 (compatible with current prompts).
Rohit Singh: we should also enable strict tenant isolation so cross-tenant noisy neighbor doesn't bleed. I'm looking at the allocator logs now.
Sam Patel: pinging account team — prepping customer comms. will tell them we may force a temporary model variant to maintain availability.
Oncall SRE: taking commands now. first step: isolate affected nodes from LB pool, then trigger tenant override. I'm going to run the control-plane change and post the command.
Oncall SRE: exec:
```
# isolate nodes
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/v1/pools/dedicated-us-west-2/actions/safe_drain -d '{"pool_id":"orion-dedicated-pool-usw2","node_filter":"oom_restart>1"}'

# tenant override (pin model)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://control-plane.internal/v1/tenants/orion-prod/overrides -d '{"override_id":"ephemeral-orion-fallback","model":"orion/safe-1.3","reason":"auto-fallback due to pool instability","expires_in":"PT30M"}'
```
Alice Ng: running the drain now.
Carla Diaz: note: safe-1.3 is 4-bit quantized and removes a custom tokenizer plugin — should be drop-in for most pipelines but watch for subtle scoring changes.
Ben Turner: started the tenant override via console UI as well (double-check). After override, route should go to compatible runtime. I'll post the API response: success, 202, override_id=ephemeral-orion-fallback.
Oncall SRE: override reflected. immediate error rate down to ~1.2% for orion-prod, tail latency 800ms. marking mitigation active.
Rohit Singh: allocator shows 2 nodes still flapping. I'll cordon them. Also enabling aggressive autoscale on the dedicated pool to spin up warm nodes (burst capacity enabled for this enterprise account).
Sam Patel: I sent the customer a quick note: "We've detected degraded performance in the dedicated pool for your tenant; we applied a temporary, lower-latency model variant to maintain availability. We're actively remediating and will follow up within 30 minutes." customer acked, thanks message.
Alice Ng: creating incident ticket INC-2026-OR-487 and linking this thread. tagging product and infra. putting postmortem guard rails: collect KV cache metrics, model version metrics, and token-level error traces.
Carla Diaz: follow-up action: schedule controlled rollback plan to restore pinned model to previous (orion/v1.4) only after validation pass on a canary set. We need quality-check prompts.
Ben Turner: handing off to Ben (next shift) at 04:30Z — I'll keep watching for 15 minutes then drop.
Oncall SRE: Ben acknowledged. next steps for Ben: monitor flapping nodes, ensure cordon/drain completed, confirm autoscale fills warm nodes, and prepare to revert tenant override when pool stable.
Ben Turner: taking over. quick status: mitigation active, customer notified, override expires in 25m (auto expiry). I'll extend if needed or convert to manual ticketed override.
Rohit Singh: adding short-term telemetry: enable token-level sampling for orion-prod for next 1h so we can detect regressions from safe-1.3.
Carla Diaz: also recommend creating a permanent fallback policy for enterprise/VPC customers: a policy that specifies safe variants and max allowed quality drift, plus an approval flow (CS + SRE) for non-auto fallbacks.
Sam Patel: noted — I'll own the comms and post-incident customer summary.
Alice Ng: patch notes and follow-ups: (1) postmortem, (2) schedule capacity increase for dedicated pool ORION, (3) add automated test harness for quantized fallback compatibility.
Oncall SRE: closing active page. monitoring remains open. will update ticket with timeline. if error rate increases >2% or latency >1.5s re-open paging.
Ben Turner: confirmed back to baseline after 20m. leaving monitoring hooks. moving to postmortem drafting.
Sam Patel: customer happy with the quick mitigation, asked for long-term SLA assurance. scheduling an account call next week.
Carla Diaz: adding snippet for future runbook to set tenant override manually via admin UI (for oncall):
```
1) Console -> Tenants -> orion-prod -> Overrides
2) Create override: model=orion/safe-1.3, reason=pool instability, expires=30m
3) Validate: run `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/orion-prod/health` and check model field
```
Oncall SRE: leaving final note — root cause appears to be a GPU kernel upgrade that increased OOM for certain sequence-length distributions. infra/ML runtime will coordinate a rollback of that kernel and a controlled re-upgrade later.
Alice Ng: thanks all. closing thread when postmortem link added to ticket. :white_check_mark:
